references.text: Laying of hands on the head of the sacrificial animal as a symbolic act of identification with the offering
The elders lay their hands on the head of the sin offering, the same ritual action as with the scapegoat
Confession of sins as part of the atonement ritual
Confession of iniquities (עֲוֺנֹת) and unfaithfulness as part of repentance
Confession of sin and guilt before atonement
The Lord's suffering servant bears the iniquities of all, a prophetic fulfillment of scapegoat symbolism
The servant bore the sins of many, parallel to the goat that carries away the people's sins
Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many, fulfilling the ritual of the Day of Atonement
The annual sacrifices could not completely remove sins, but pointed forward to Christ's perfect offering
Christ bore our sins in his body on the tree, fulfilling the scapegoat typology
Confession of sins leads to forgiveness and cleansing, continuing the principle of confession
